prose_updates.tldr: Adding parents to a supplied rooted tree creates finite ambiguity measured here by the single-coordinate complex degree \(D_k(n)\), not by whole-fiber cardinality or real root count. The paper proves the universal \(2^{k+1}\) ceiling, the equality \(D_k(n)=2^{k+1}\) for \(n\geq2k+4\), the inherited all-size lower envelope, and the exact frontier for every \(n\leq5\). The only unresolved frontier region is \(k>0\), \(n\geq6\), and \(n<2k+4\). Because \(\mathcal G_{n,0}\) is exactly the published tree class, the unconditional dispatcher retains its complete \(1/2/\infty\) classification and finite expressions at zero excess; positive excess currently receives an exact algebraic-versus-transcendental Jacobian tag and degree ceiling. Exact positive-excess polynomials, exceptional sets, real lifting, and regular inference are proved on the supplied-valid-chart and successful-output domain of the conditional geometric-resolution theorem.

project_justification.gap: The published tree algorithms completely solve exactly \(\mathcal G_{n,0}\), not \(\mathcal G_{n,k}\) for positive \(k\). General mixed-graph work studies rational recovery, whole-parameter fibers, or unparameterized elimination, and does not give the maximum finite degree of one original directed coefficient as a function of both vertex size and excess-parent budget. General geometric-resolution algorithms also do not select the embedded SEM source prime or provide bounded descent over the implicitly presented covariance field.
project_justification.niche: Distance from a supplied arborescence creates a parameterized algebraic regime in which the orientation system yields a projection-aware ceiling and explicit constructions yield sharp size-sensitive lower bounds. The zero-excess class inherits a complete published algorithm, while positive excess separates the unconditional algebraicity tag from chart-certified exact finite output.
project_justification.fill: The paper proves the projection-aware degree upper bound, the large-size equality, the inherited all-size lower envelope, and the exact \(n\leq5\) coordinate-degree frontier. It isolates the remaining positive-\(k\), \(n\geq6\) small-size frontier in \(\mathrm{oeq:sharp\mbox{-}size\mbox{-}frontier}\). It supplies an unconditional randomized Jacobian-rank tag, retains the complete published tree-case output at \(k=0\), and proves a conditional geometric-resolution theorem with explicit straight-line-program and intermediate-degree dependence. Exceptional-set, real-lifting, and regular-inference results hold only on the supplied-valid-chart and successful-output domain.

prose_updates.related_work: Van der Zander, Wienöbst, Bläser, and Liśkiewicz introduced TreeID for tree-shaped linear SEMs; Gupta and Bläser proved the complete per-parameter \(1/2/\infty\) classification and finite-expression algorithm, and Briefs and Bläser accelerated the same tree-only predicate in fasttreeid. That published tree class is exactly \(\mathcal G_{n,0}\), up to a harmless vertex-count indexing shift, and is not \(\mathcal G_{n,k}\) for positive \(k\). Foygel, Draisma, and Drton give the published five-node whole-fiber cubic used here as the \(D_1(5)\) base case; their cubic and other small higher-degree examples are not novelty claims. Hollering, Misra, and Sturma optimize bounded-degree rational formulas, which is a different degree notion. Giusti, Lecerf, and Salvy compute geometric resolutions for reduced regular sequences away from an inequation, and Lecerf treats arbitrary equations and inequations with complexity charged to intermediate geometric degree; neither selects the embedded source component or manufactures its source-nonzero chart. The exceptional-set, real-lifting, regular-cell, root-separation, finite-set, and singleton-inference results are proved only after a valid chart and successful conditional output are supplied; they cover every retained branch without claiming discriminant-uniform inference or automatic branch selection.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The exact frontier is still unknown only for positive \(k\), \(n\geq6\), and \(n<2k+4\): the orientation coefficient may lose branches through forced covariance relations, exact localization, affine dehomogenization, or projective infinity. The exhaustive five-node orbit census is now a secondary regression and coordinate-census question, not a kill test for the numerical frontier, because the cubic and quartic base cases and the entire \(n\leq5\) frontier are fixed. Independently, the quadratic core does not construct a reduced local presentation of the embedded source prime or bounded rational-circuit descent over \(K_G\). The exceptional-set theorem, real-root-lifting theorem, regular-cell lemma, derived root-separation lemma, regular finite-set inference theorem, and singleton inference proposition are proved conditional on a supplied valid chart and successful conditional output; none is claimed unconditionally. Coordinate localization is never promoted to equality of full fibers, real roots are never equated with real supported lifts, and local rank is not used to assert real uniqueness.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The paper proves the full frontier through five vertices, the all-size lower envelope, and the large-size equality, but not the remaining positive-excess small-size strip. Unconditionally, the dispatcher returns the complete published \(1/2/\infty\) classification and finite \(\operatorname{FASTP}\) expressions on \(\mathcal G_{n,0}\). For \(|D\setminus T|>0\), it returns only a randomized algebraic-versus-transcendental tag, a rank or dominance certificate, and the degree ceiling; it does not return \(d_e(G)\), \(p_e\), \(\mathcal Q_{G,e}\), or \(h_{G,e}\) on the algebraic branch. Given valid source-prime charts and successful output, the conditional geometric-resolution theorem returns those exact finite objects with its stated straight-line-program and intermediate-degree dependence. On precisely that same conditional domain, the six exceptional-set, real-lifting, and regular-inference results are proved. No discriminant-uniform inference, automatic branch selection, or all-singular-covariance guarantee is claimed, and positive definiteness of recovered noise follows only after a complete real supported lift by congruence.
